$comment: Meta-schema of the emission classification registries (bridge/protocol/openclaw/emissions/<version>.json). This file DOCUMENTS the shape; test/emissions-coverage.test.ts ENFORCES it (the enums below are asserted equal to the test's own constants). The registry classifies the emission inventory of the same version (protocol/openclaw/<version>/agent-emissions.json): every (stream, phase) pair under `streams.<stream>.phases`, every data key an emission row (or a gateway-fabricated frame) writes under `streams.<stream>.keys`, and every key a gateway rewrite adds after emission under `rewrites` (`<scope>:<function>:<key>`). Text forms are the inventory's: `-` = no phase key, `<opaque>` = a value the derivation could not resolve. Statuses: handled = Atrium reads it, with an `anchor` present in the comment-stripped bridge source (the coverage-truth rule) and a `proof` (a golden-corpus scenario that carries it, or a deterministic test that names it, with the reason the corpus cannot); gap = a known defect, named by its identifier (`gap`, e.g. F1) with its impact (`note`); ignored = a deliberate exclusion (`why`) — a why that describes a breakage is a gap.

proof.$comment: golden-corpus: `ref` is a scenario of this version's corpus, or `<version>/<scenario>` of another vendored corpus; the test checks the capture carries the pair or key. deterministic-test: `ref` is a bridge test file that names the phase or key, `note` says why no capture shows it.
